html.La curva di Mauna Loa non misura quanto: The Mauna Loa curve does not measure what we emit. It measures what is left over after the oceans and vegetation have taken their share. Every year they absorb about half of it, for free.
html.<b>Le unità di questa pagina.</b> <abbr: The units on this page. GtCO₂ = billions of tonnes of CO₂. ppm = molecules of CO₂ per million molecules of air. Sink = whatever takes CO₂ out of the air: the ocean and vegetation. CO₂e = all greenhouse gases converted into the amount of CO₂ that would warm the same; used where methane and nitrous oxide count, as in the section on wars. Averages for 2015–2024 from the Global Carbon Budget 2025.

html.Le bolle intrappolate nel ghiaccio antar: The bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice are real air from eight hundred thousand years ago, and it can be measured. In all that time CO₂ swung between 170 and 300 parts per million, back and forth, with the ice ages. Never once above.
html.Ottocentomila anni di respiro, e poi noi: Eight hundred thousand years of breathing, and then us
html.Concentrazione di CO₂ dalle carote di gh: CO₂ concentration from Antarctic ice cores up to 1958, then the annual means from Mauna Loa. The horizontal axis is linear: each pixel is worth about a thousand years, so the whole industrial era fits in less than one pixel. The vertical line on the right is not a drawing error.
html.<b>Il dente di sega sono le ere glaciali: The sawtooth is the ice ages, eight cycles of about a hundred thousand years each: CO₂ fell to 180 ppm as the ice advanced and climbed back to 280 as it retreated, always together with temperature. The vertical line on the right is us: the same distance covered in two hundred years instead of ten thousand, and climbing past the ceiling of the whole record.
html.Nessun essere umano ha mai respirato que: No human being has ever breathed this air
html.I fossili più antichi della nostra speci: The oldest fossils of our species are about 315,000 years old. In all that time CO₂ never went above 300 parts per million: today we are at 427. This is not a figure of speech, it is the record right here. Everything we call human history happened in the right-hand part of the chart, where the line is flat.
html.Più indietro si va, meno si misura: The further back you go, the less is measured
html.Il ghiaccio arriva a ottocentomila anni:: The ice reaches eight hundred thousand years: beyond that, ancient air no longer exists and you move to indirect indicators, which carry much wider uncertainties. The IPCC says today's CO₂ is the highest in at least two million years; a 2023 synthesis of the whole Cenozoic places the last time at this level around fourteen million years ago. Three different rulers, three answers: the measured one comes first.
html.Approfondisci: com'era il mondo l'ultima: Go deeper: what the world was like the last time CO₂ was this high
html.Periodi di riferimento del paleoclima, v: Palaeoclimate reference periods, IPCC AR6 values relative to 1850–1900
html.Ultimo massimo glaciale · 20 mila anni f: Last glacial maximum · 20 thousand years ago
html.Il Pliocene non è una previsione: The Pliocene is not a forecast
html.È la riga che conta, perché la CO₂ di al: It is the row that matters, because the CO₂ back then is the CO₂ of today: between 360 and 420 ppm, for a long stretch. The world that came with it was 2.5–4 °C warmer and had the sea between 5 and 25 metres higher. But those values are equilibrium states, reached over millennia. The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets take thousands of years to respond, and the Pliocene tells you where the planet ends up if CO₂ stays there, not what happens by 2100. Projections for this century are another matter and give tens of centimetres, not tens of metres.
html.Perché le ere glaciali non sono un'obiez: Why the ice ages are not an objection
html.«La CO₂ è già cambiata da sola in passat: «CO₂ has changed on its own before» is true, and you can see it clearly in the chart. Those cycles start from changes in the Earth's orbit, which by themselves move little energy: it is the CO₂ released by warming oceans that amplifies them into an ice age. The difference with today is the cause and the speed: those transitions added 100 ppm in about ten thousand years, we have added 140 in two hundred.
html.Le carote di ghiaccio sono misure dirett: Ice cores are direct measurements of the air and reach eight hundred thousand years. To go further you need indirect indicators, such as boron in the shells of foraminifera: the IPCC, in 2021, concludes from these that current CO₂ is the highest in at least two million years. The Cenozoic synthesis published in Science in 2023 revised the reconstruction of the last 66 million years and places the last period with CO₂ steadily at these levels around fourteen million years ago. The number that often circulates, «three million years», comes from earlier reconstructions.
html.Gli ultimi dieci anni, da vicino: The last ten years, up close
html.Sulla curva lunga un singolo anno non si: On the long curve a single year is indistinguishable. Here it is not: and you can see that the years when CO₂ rose the most, 2016, 2023 and 2024, are the same years when the planet was warmest.
html.Gli anni caldi sono gli anni in cui sale: The warm years are the years it rises most
html.Gli ultimi dieci anni, tre pannelli sull: The last ten years, three panels on the same time axis. Top: monthly means from Mauna Loa (thin line), the underlying rise once the seasonal breathing of plants is removed (thick line) and the annual means (dots). Middle: how much CO₂ grew in each year, from 1 January to 31 December; the solid bars are the years above average. Bottom: global temperature in the same year.
html.<b>Gli anni in cui la CO₂ cresce di più: The years when CO₂ grows most are the warm years: 2016, 2023, 2024. It is not the temperature that produces the extra CO₂: it is El Niño, the periodic warming of the Pacific, which warms the planet and dries the tropics at the same time, so vegetation absorbs less. Once El Niño ended, growth in 2025 was back to 2.2 ppm.
html.Perché due numeri diversi per lo stesso: Why two different numbers for the same year
html.«Cresciuta di 2,23 ppm» è il tasso NOAA:: «Grew by 2.23 ppm» is the NOAA rate: how much the underlying curve rises between 1 January and 31 December. The difference between one year's mean and the previous year's gives a slightly different number (in 2024: 3.53 against 3.33), because an annual mean contains half of the previous year. This page always uses the NOAA rate.
html.E allora? Cosa fanno quei ppm: So what? What those ppm actually do
html.Finora abbiamo contato molecole. Più CO₂: So far we have been counting molecules. More CO₂ in the air means less heat escaping to space: this is the same chart as before, measured in degrees.
html.Il pianeta si è già scaldato di circa 1,: The planet has already warmed by about 1.3 degrees
html.Di quanto ogni anno è stato più caldo de: How much warmer each year was than the 1850–1900 average, land and oceans together (NOAAGlobalTemp). It is the same baseline the 1.5 °C goal refers to.
html.<b>Un anno sopra 1,5 °C non è la soglia: One year above 1.5 °C is not the threshold crossed. The limit is judged on underlying warming, that is on an average of several years: here it is the last ten, today 1.18 °C. The Paris Agreement does not prescribe how many years, and the IPCC uses twenty. A single warm year can be pushed up by El Niño, as in 2024; a cooler year takes nothing back, as in 2025: it is the same post-El Niño return seen in CO₂, and the underlying trend has not changed. The budget in the data box is how much we can still emit for a 50% chance of staying below 1.5 °C: 170 GtCO₂ from the start of 2026, minus the months already gone.
html.<b>Il 2025 è più fresco del 2024, e non: 2025 is cooler than 2024, and that is not good news. It is the same post-El Niño return seen in CO₂: the underlying trend has not changed.
html.Un anno sopra 1,5 °C non è la soglia sup: One year above 1.5 °C is not the threshold crossed
html.Il limite si giudica sul riscaldamento d: The limit is judged on underlying warming, that is on an average of several years: here it is the last ten, today 1.18 °C. The Paris Agreement does not prescribe how many years, and the IPCC uses twenty. A single warm year can be pushed up by El Niño, as in 2024; a cooler year takes nothing back, as in 2025. The budget in the data box is how much we can still emit for a 50% chance of staying below 1.5 °C: 170 GtCO₂ from the start of 2026, minus the months already gone.
html.la cifra a cui si riferisce il limite di: the figure the 1.5 °C limit refers to
html.per il 50% di probabilità di restare sot: for a 50% chance of staying below: 3.3 years at the current rate, not a date
html.Approfondisci: i termometri non sono d'a: Go deeper: the thermometers disagree, and CO₂ is not alone
html.Un decimo di grado di disaccordo fra i t: A tenth of a degree of disagreement between thermometers
html.Questa pagina usa NOAAGlobalTemp. Altre: This page uses NOAAGlobalTemp. Other authoritative series — ERA5 from Copernicus, HadCRUT from the Met Office, Berkeley Earth — give values between 1.5 and 1.6 °C for 2024 (ERA5 1.60; the World Meteorological Organization synthesis 1.55). The same NOAA series, in its previous version, gave 1.46: the 2025 revision lowered recent values by a few hundredths. The difference comes from how each one covers the areas without stations, above all the Arctic, and from how it estimates the pre-industrial period, for which measurements are few. When you read «we have passed 1.5 °C», it is worth asking with which ruler.
html.E non c'è solo l'anidride carbonica: And carbon dioxide is not alone
html.media globale NOAA, +52% sul preindustri: NOAA global mean, +52% above pre-industrial; Mauna Loa, further north, reads slightly higher
html.ppb = parti per miliardo · +168% sul pre: ppb = parts per billion · +168% above pre-industrial (722)
html.Il metano è molto più raro ma, molecola: Methane is far rarer but, molecule for molecule, it traps much more heat than CO₂ in the short term; in exchange it breaks down within about ten years, while a fraction of CO₂ stays for centuries. That is why cutting methane works fast and cutting CO₂ works forever: both are needed, and they are not interchangeable.
html.Dove finisce quello che emettiamo: Where what we emit ends up
html.Il bilancio globale del carbonio ha due: The global carbon budget has two sides. On the left what we put in, on the right the three possible destinations. Only the third one shows up in the curve.
html.Metà di quello che emettiamo sparisce in: Half of what we emit disappears into ocean and vegetation
html.Bilancio globale del carbonio, media ann: Global carbon budget, annual average 2015–2024, in billions of tonnes of CO₂. Fossil fuels net of the small share that cement reabsorbs. 1 ppm = 7.78 GtCO₂.
html.<b>I baffi sotto i blocchi sono l'incert: The whiskers under the blocks are the uncertainty. The land sink is worth 8.7 GtCO₂ but is known to within ±2.9, a third of it; we know the ocean twice as well. Over the decade average the budget balances; in a single year it does not, and 2024 is the most glaring case.
html.Se i pozzi smettessero di funzionare dom: If the sinks stopped working tomorrow, with the same emissions the concentration would rise by 5.3 ppm a year instead of 2.6. Half the problem is already being swept under the carpet by oceans and forests. Per person that is about 5 tonnes a year, the weight of three cars.
html.Global Carbon Budget 2025, medie 2015–20: Global Carbon Budget 2025, 2015–2024 averages converted into GtCO₂
html.Il lavoro che i pozzi hanno già fatto: The work the sinks have already done
html.Un modo per vedere quanto valgono oceano: One way to see what ocean and vegetation are worth: draw where the curve would be if they had absorbed nothing.
html.Senza i pozzi saremmo a 574 ppm, non a 4: Without the sinks we would be at 574 ppm, not 427
html.La curva tratteggiata somma al valore de: The dashed curve adds to the 1959 value all the emissions accumulated since then. The gap between the two lines is the CO₂ that oceans and vegetation have taken out of the air, for free, in sixty-six years.
html.<span class=\"sw sw-cf\"></span>Se nessu: If no sink had absorbed anything
html.<b>147 ppm di differenza.</b> È più di q: 147 ppm of difference. That is more than the concentration has risen in the whole observed period. Put another way: of the roughly 258 ppm we have put in since 1959, we see 111 in the air — the rest is in the ocean and in vegetation. The calculation assumes all emissions had stayed in the atmosphere; it is an accounting comparison, not a simulation of the climate that would have followed.
html.Il servizio gratuito, a tariffa crescent: The free service, at a rising price
html.Finora i pozzi hanno assorbito <em>di pi: So far the sinks have absorbed more as we emitted more: more CO₂ in the air means more pressure pushing the gas into the ocean and more fertilisation of vegetation. But the Global Carbon Budget 2025 estimates that warming has already weakened the land sink by 25% and the ocean sink by 7% compared with a world that had not warmed.
html.Perché il 2024 dipende da dove guardi: Why 2024 depends on where you look
html.Nel 2024 le emissioni sono cresciute di: In 2024 emissions grew by about 1%. At Mauna Loa CO₂ rose as much as the year before; in the global mean it made the biggest jump since the series began, in 1980. This is not a contradiction: they are two different instruments, and a single year is not enough to judge.
html.Lo stesso anno, misurato in due modi: The same year, measured two ways
html.Tasso di crescita annuo della CO₂. <span: Annual growth rate of CO₂. Mauna Loa is a single observatory in the Pacific; the global mean is computed from stations far from cities and industry, combined so that each band of the planet weighs as much as its surface.
html.<b>Nel 2023 Mauna Loa correva più del pi: In 2023 Mauna Loa was running faster than the planet, in 2024 the opposite. A single observatory depends on how the winds bring it air: excellent for the long trend, less so for judging a single year. When someone quotes «2024 did X ppm», they should say which of the two measures they are using.
html.Perché non fidarsi di un solo anno: Why you should not trust a single year
html.<b>Il 2023 e il 2024 sono stati eccezion: 2023 and 2024 were exceptional for a reason that has nothing to do with our emissions: El Niño dried the tropics and fed record fires, and vegetation absorbed less. The land sink held 7.4 GtCO₂ in 2023 and 7.1 in 2024, against a decade average of 8.7. The ocean, far more stable, carried on doing its job.
html.Approfondisci: il 2024 che non torna, e: Go deeper: the 2024 that does not add up, and how it ended in 2025
html.Per il 2024 il bilancio non torna: somma: For 2024 the budget does not add up: summing what ended in the air, in the sea and in vegetation gives more than what appears to have been emitted, with a gap of 6 GtCO₂, the most negative in the series. The Global Carbon Project publishes it as an item of its own. In 2025 growth fell to 2.23 ppm at Mauna Loa and 2.06 in the global mean, and the preliminary Global Carbon Budget estimate indicates that the land sink is back to its former strength. The anomaly was a swing, not a break: building a thesis on 2024 alone would be unwise in either direction.
html.Chi emette, in tre letture diverse: Who emits, in three different readings
html.Sono tre domande distinte e danno tre ri: These are three distinct questions and they give three distinct answers. All three are needed: who emits most today, who emits most per person, and who filled the tub.
html.Un terzo delle emissioni viene dalla Cin: A third of emissions comes from China. Per person and cumulatively, the ranking changes
html.Emissioni da fossili e cemento, escluso: Emissions from fossil fuels and cement, excluding land use (Global Carbon Budget 2025 via Our World in Data). Each panel has its own scale: compare positions, not lengths across panels.
html.miliardi di tonnellate di CO₂ e quota su: billions of tonnes of CO₂ and share of the world total
html.tonnellate di CO₂ all'anno per abitante: tonnes of CO₂ per inhabitant per year
html.% del carbonio fossile totale mai emesso: % of all fossil carbon ever emitted
html.Totale mondiale <b>38,6 GtCO₂</b> nel 20: World total 38.6 GtCO₂ in 2024: China alone accounts for almost a third, Italy for less than 1%. The cumulative figure is the reading that matters for the climate: the CO₂ emitted in 1950 is still up there. Which number to quote: 38.6 is fossil fuels alone for one year; the 40.9 at the top of the page is the 2015–2024 average including land use.
html.Approfondisci: da quali combustibili e d: Go deeper: from which fuels and from which uses
html.Da dove arriva la CO₂ fossile · mondo 20: Where fossil CO₂ comes from · world 2023 (fuels: Global Carbon Budget; end uses: IEA estimates)
html.Gli usi finali seguono la classificazion: End uses follow the IEA classification: electricity is counted where it is produced, not where it is consumed. With the economic-sector breakdown used by the IPCC the same emissions give different percentages, because industry and buildings take back their share of electricity.
html.Altro, incluso il gas bruciato ai pozzi: Other, including gas flared at wells
html.No per il livello, in buona parte sì per: No for the level, largely yes for the growth. China accounts for a third of today's total. Of the increase over the last twenty-five years it accounts for about two thirds, because in the meantime Europe and the United States have come down.
html.Dal 2000 la Cina spiega due terzi dell'a: Since 2000 China explains two thirds of the increase
html.Quanto è cambiato dal 2000 al 2024 il co: How much each one's contribution changed from 2000 to 2024, in billions of tonnes of CO₂ per year.
html.Resto del mondo e trasporti internaziona: Rest of the world and international transport
html.Saldo netto mondiale <b>+13,1 GtCO₂</b>,: World net balance +13.1 GtCO₂, from 25.5 to 38.6. China alone covers about two thirds of that net increase.
html.<b>La prima:</b> «netto» nasconde qualco: The first: «net» hides something. Europe and the United States also came down by moving production to China itself. Counted on consumption rather than production, a sizeable slice of Chinese emissions is goods destined for us, and the European fall gets much thinner.
html.<b>La seconda:</b> il quadro si ribalta: The second: the picture flips if you look at the carbon already accumulated instead of the annual flow. There the Western contribution is still the largest, and will stay so for a good while.
html.Due risposte controintuitive. Gli eserci: Two counter-intuitive answers. Armies in peacetime emit far more than the wars they fight. And inside a war the weapons weigh almost nothing: what counts is what they hit, and what then has to be rebuilt. These are the least solid estimates on this page, and they are floors, not measurements.
html.Le armi sono l'1%: il resto è ciò che co: Weapons are 1%: the rest is what they hit
html.Gas serra in milioni di tonnellate di CO: Greenhouse gases in millions of tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. On the left the total for each case, over different periods indicated under each item; on the right where that total comes from in the war in Iran, the most recent breakdown available. Each panel has its own scale.
html.Quanto pesa in tutto: How much it weighs in total
html.attenzione al periodo: cambia da voce a: mind the period: it changes from item to item
html.Eserciti del mondo<small>ogni anno, guer: The world's armies<small>every year, wars excluded</small>
html.<span class=\"tag tag-prel\">stima preli: preliminary estimate war in Iran, 28 February – 14 March 2026
html.<b>In due settimane di guerra in Iran i: In two weeks of war in Iran the missiles and drones are worth 55 thousand tonnes of CO₂e, the buildings hit and the oil burned four million three hundred thousand: almost eighty times as much. That is why you do not do the accounting of a war by counting munitions. Mind what these totals include: in Ukraine 73 of the 311 million tonnes are the reconstruction still to come, in Gaza 31 out of 33, and military operations alone in Gaza are worth 1.3. They are not in the atmosphere yet: they are attributed to the war that will make them necessary.
html.Perché sono minimi, non misure: Why they are floors, not measurements
html.Gli eserciti non dichiarano: le prime es: Armies do not report: the first exemptions came with the Kyoto Protocol in 1997, since 2015 the Paris Agreement makes reporting voluntary, and the United States, China and Russia do not publish complete data. The accounting of wars is done by researchers from the outside, event by event, and covers only what can be documented. For Syria, Yemen and Sudan no total exists. From vegetation fires alone, in the sixteen countries with ongoing or recent conflicts, 1,456 MtCO₂e went into the air in 2020: not all of it caused by war, but attributed to nobody.
html.Durante la guerra le emissioni dichiarat: During the war the emissions declared by Syria fell, because oil production collapsed by more than a quarter. Meanwhile the damage was piling up elsewhere: putting the destroyed houses back up alone is worth about 22 MtCO₂, and it will arrive in the years of reconstruction. In official accounts a war can look like a climate policy.
html.Approfondisci: da cosa nascono le emissi: Go deeper: where the emissions of a war come from
html.Quattro anni di guerra in Ucraina, 24 fe: Four years of war in Ukraine, 24 February 2022 – 23 February 2026
html.Carburante di mezzi e aerei, munizioni: Fuel for vehicles and aircraft, munitions
html.Cemento e acciaio per rifare ciò che è d: Cement and steel to rebuild what is destroyed
html.Boschi e campi bruciati: 1,39 milioni di: Woods and fields burned: 1.39 million hectares in 2025 alone
html.Voli deviati intorno allo spazio aereo c: Flights diverted around the closed airspace
html.Il quarto anno da solo vale 75: The fourth year alone is worth 75
html.Anche in Ucraina le armi sono la parte p: In Ukraine too the weapons are the small part
html.I combattimenti sono poco più di un terz: Fighting is little more than a third of the total. The rest is what the war drags behind it: rebuilding, failing to put out the fires, diverting aircraft, moving people. Reconstruction alone weighs almost as much as the fighting, and grows as the destruction piles up. At 185 dollars a tonne, the climate damage Ukraine intends to claim exceeds 57 billion.
html.Israele e Gaza: il 93% è il dopo: Israel and Gaza: 93% is the aftermath
html.Lo stesso schema, ancora più netto. Le o: The same pattern, even sharper. Military operations are worth a little over 1.3 MtCO₂e up to January 2025; the total reaches 33.2 counting the barriers built before and the reconstruction to come: almost 450 thousand flats, over 3,000 kilometres of roads, schools, hospitals, water systems. If the number looks small next to Ukraine it is because the territory is tiny and the count of operations is narrow: it covers flights and vehicles, not every building that burned.
html.Iran: cosa è stato colpito, e cosa manca: Iran: what was hit, and what the count is missing
html.Una trentina di impianti di lavorazione: Around thirty oil processing and storage plants in Iran, plus refineries and tankers outside the country: that is where the 1.88 million tonnes of the «oil burned» item come from. The count covers the first two weeks and has not yet been through a scientific journal: we have marked it as a preliminary estimate in the chart. Take it for the order of magnitude and for the proportions between items, not for the exact figure.
html.Nel 1991, ritirandosi dal Kuwait, l'eser: In 1991, retreating from Kuwait, the Iraqi army set fire to hundreds of oil wells. Those fires alone were worth more than 2% of all the fossil CO₂ emitted in the world that year: more than four years of war in Ukraine have produced. It is the limiting case that explains why hitting energy, rather than people, is what weighs most on the climate.
html.Ogni 100 miliardi di dollari di spesa mi: Every 100 billion dollars of extra military spending is worth about 32 MtCO₂e a year. The increase in NATO spending between 2019 and 2024 has already added around sixty, and the announced increases would bring another 132: as much as the fossil emissions of a country like Chile, every year. The figures have a wide margin, the sign does not.
html.Perché Kyoto non ha piegato la curva: Why Kyoto did not bend the curve
html.Il protocollo non era progettato per fer: The protocol was not designed to stop the growth. And even if it had worked perfectly, the concentration would have risen anyway.
html.Fra la firma e la fine del primo periodo: Between the signature and the end of the first period, emissions rose by 43%
html.Emissioni fossili mondiali 1990–2024, in: World fossil emissions 1990–2024, in billions of tonnes of CO₂. The band marks the 2008–2012 commitment period.
html.<b>La vasca si riempie comunque.</b> Son: The tub fills up anyway. These are fossil fuels alone, year by year. Kyoto bound a subset of countries to cut by 5%; between 1997 and 2012 the rest of the world grew by over 60%, and the countries without commitments doubled. The only visible drop is 2020, and no treaty deserves the credit.
html.La CO₂ atmosferica è uno stock, non un f: Atmospheric CO₂ is a stock, not a flow. It is a tub filling up: closing the tap halfway does not lower the level, it makes it rise more slowly. To stop the growth you need net zero emissions, that is not putting in more than the sinks take out: emitting less is not enough. Kyoto asked for minus 5.2% relative to 1990, for a subset of countries.
html.Approfondisci: la cronologia di Kyoto, e: Go deeper: the chronology of Kyoto, and what it left behind
html.Obiettivo: meno 5,2% rispetto al 1990 pe: Target: minus 5.2% relative to 1990 for industrialised countries only, by 2008–2012. China, India and Brazil have no commitments.
html.Gli Stati Uniti non ratificano: The United States does not ratify
html.Il primo emettitore del mondo all'epoca: The largest emitter in the world at the time stays out. The treaty covers less than a third of global emissions, a share falling year by year.
html.Nel frattempo le emissioni globali sono: In the meantime global emissions have already risen from 24.4 to 29.6 GtCO₂ compared with the year of the signature.
html.Per evitare le sanzioni previste dal man: To avoid the penalties foreseen for missing the target.
html.I paesi vincolati centrano l'obiettivo,: The bound countries meet the target, but most of the fall comes from the post-1991 collapse of ex-Soviet industry and from offshoring, not from climate policy.
html.Kyoto non è stato inutile. Ha creato gli: Kyoto was not useless. It created the national inventories, the measurement and verification systems and the carbon markets, including the European emissions trading scheme (ETS). It is the infrastructure on which the Paris Agreement was then built. What it did not do is reverse or halt the growth of world emissions, and indeed it did not stop the rise of CO₂ in the atmosphere: precisely in the Kyoto years the concentration kept accelerating, from 1.5 to 2.0 ppm a year between the 1990s and the following decade. These are two separate accounts, and they should be kept separate. What would bend the curve: net zero emissions, not reduced emissions. That is the goal the Paris Agreement later set for mid-century.
html.Se di questa pagina resta una schermata,: If one screen of this page is all that stays with you, let it be this one. The numbers below update together with those in the previous sections.
html.<b>La CO₂ in aria è a <span data-from=\": CO₂ in the air is at 427.35 ppm, 53% above the pre-industrial level, and it is rising by about 2.6 ppm a year: three times faster than in the 1960s.
html.<b>Ogni anno emettiamo circa 41 miliardi: Every year we emit about 41 billion tonnes; half disappears into ocean and vegetation. The curve measures only the other half. Without the sinks we would be at 574 ppm instead of 427.
html.<b>Il pianeta si è scaldato di <span dat: The planet warmed by +1.29 °C in the last year, +1.18 on average over the last decade. The Paris limit, 1.5 °C, is judged on an average of several years, not on a single one: it has not been passed yet, and about 140 GtCO₂ remain for a 50% chance of staying below it, less than four years of emissions at the current rate.
html.<b>Gli anni caldi sono gli anni in cui l: The warm years are the years when CO₂ rises most. In 2023 and 2024 El Niño weakened vegetation and growth reached 3.3 ppm. A single year makes no trend, in either direction.
html.<b>Chi emette dipende dalla domanda.</b>: Who emits depends on the question. Today China emits a third of the total, but an American emits one and a half times a Chinese person each, and over a hundred and seventy years the United States and Europe filled the tub more than anyone. Cutting slows the rise; to stop it you need net zero emissions.

In November the Global Carbon Budget comes out, with the year's emissions and the estimate of the sinks: those numbers have to be updated by hand in the budget sections. At any time: the state of El Niño, because a new warm event would push CO₂ growth back up without emissions having changed.

html.Il <b>tasso di crescita</b> NOAA è l'aum: The NOAA growth rate is the increase between 1 January and 31 December, computed on the thick line of the charts, the one without the seasonal breathing. The difference between annual means is another thing and gives different numbers: in 2024, 3.33 ppm the first, 3.53 the second. Also, Mauna Loa is not the planet: it is an observatory at 3,400 metres in the Pacific, while the NOAA global mean is computed from marine stations far from cities and industry, where the air is well mixed, combined so that each latitude band weighs as much as its surface. In 2024 the two measures give 3.33 and 3.76 ppm.
html.Le <b>GtC</b> (miliardi di tonnellate di: The GtC (billions of tonnes of carbon) that appear in scientific publications convert into GtCO₂ by multiplying by 3.664: this page always uses GtCO₂.
html.Cosa è cambiato in questa pagina: il reg: What has changed on this page: the revision log
html.La scienza del clima si corregge, e ques: Climate science corrects itself, and this page does the same. The most recent entries are at the top.
html.<b>Aggiunti gli ottocentomila anni.</b>: The eight hundred thousand years added. The page was missing the long scale: now there is the series from Antarctic ice cores, where you can see that CO₂ never went above 300 ppm in eight glacial cycles, and that no human being has ever breathed today's air. With the right numbers: the record is not «three million years», a figure from superseded reconstructions, but at least two million according to the IPCC and about fourteen according to the 2023 synthesis. The Pliocene, the last epoch with this much CO₂, was +2.5 to +4 °C with the sea between 5 and 25 metres higher, not 35: and those were equilibria reached over millennia, not forecasts for 2100.
html.<b>Ogni figura dichiara che tipo di nume: Every figure declares what kind of number it shows. Observed, observed and estimated, estimate, preliminary estimate: four labels, explained below. While we were at it, some over-firm wordings were corrected. The 1.5 °C limit is not «measured on a decade average»: the Agreement does not prescribe how many years, we use ten and the IPCC twenty. The remaining budget is not a date but a 50% probability. Of Kyoto we no longer say that the effect is «essentially nil» but that it did not reverse the growth of emissions, which is what the data show. «Cutting is not enough» has become «cutting slows the rise, stopping it requires net zero emissions». In the section on wars it is now explicit that part of the totals is future reconstruction, not yet emitted.
html.<b>Aggiunta la sezione sulle guerre.</b>: The section on wars added. An answer to the most frequent question of all was missing. The first version compared only the totals; this one also shows what they are made of, because that is where the surprise is: in the first fourteen days of war in Iran the missiles are worth 1% and the buildings hit together with the burned oil 84%. The sources are four and independent of each other. The totals remain floors: armies do not report and for Syria, Yemen and Sudan no count exists at all.
html.<b>Corretti i numeri del bilancio decenn: The decade budget numbers and the budget counter corrected. An independent review re-downloaded the Global Carbon Budget 2025 CSV and found that the 2015–2024 averages on the page had been transcribed wrongly: land use 5.0 and not 5.6, ocean 11.8 and not 11.6, vegetation 8.7 and not 9.2, atmosphere 20.4 and not 19.7. The «unexplained imbalance» of 1.2 GtCO₂ over the decade does not exist: it is almost nil, while in 2024 alone it is −6 GtCO₂. The remaining budget for 1.5 °C must be counted from the start of 2026, not 2025: the counter went from 98 to about 140 GtCO₂. Country data also updated to 2024.
html.<b>Tolte le note di revisione della pres: The revision notes about the original presentation removed. The page was born to check an existing slide («425 ppm in 2020», «3 times faster», «decade after decade») and annotated its errors under the charts. Now the page is the presentation: the charts are correct, and the notes were correcting something the reader no longer sees. What was true in them has stayed in the captions and in the table by decade.
html.<b>Aggiunto lo zoom sugli ultimi dieci a: The zoom on the last ten years added. On the curve since 1959 the 2023–2024 jump is invisible: the new chart shows the recent months and, below, the growth of each single year. This one too is redrawn with the NOAA data read live.
html.<b>Aggiornata al Global Carbon Budget 20: Updated to the Global Carbon Budget 2025. The land sink was revised from 11.7 to 8.7 GtCO₂ a year and the share staying in the atmosphere rose from 45% to about 50%: the largest revision, due both to new data and to the shift of the reference decade.
html.<b>Corretta una sezione che mescolava du: A section that mixed two series corrected. The previous version spoke of a 25% jump in the 2024 growth. At Mauna Loa that jump is not there (3.32 against 3.33 ppm); it is in the global mean (2.70 against 3.76). They were two different datasets quoted as if they were one.
html.<b>Reso visibile lo squilibrio di bilanc: The budget imbalance made visible. In a single year sources and sinks, measured with independent methods, never add up exactly: the disagreement is published as an item of its own.
html.<b>Corretto il fattore di conversione</b: The conversion factor corrected from 7.82 to 7.78 GtCO₂ per ppm, which was not consistent with the value in carbon declared next to it.
html.Cosa è solido e cosa no: What is solid and what is not
html.Ogni figura porta un'etichetta che dice: Every figure carries a label saying what kind of number it is. observed are published measurements and inventories: the NOAA series, the country emissions of the Global Carbon Budget. observed and estimated is the global budget, where the fossil sources are inventories but the two sinks are reconstructed with models, which is the reason for the uncertainty whiskers under the blocks. estimate is a calculation or a model: the counterfactual without sinks, the accounting of wars. preliminary estimate is work that has not yet been through a scientific journal, and on this page it appears only once.
html.Le emissioni fossili sono note entro cir: Fossil emissions are known to within about 5%. The ocean sink to within about 15%. The land sink and land use are the worst constrained items, with uncertainties that in single years exceed 50% of the value. The budget never closes exactly: the residual imbalance is published as an item of its own, and in 2024 it reached −6 GtCO₂ (−1.7 GtC), the most negative value in the series.
html.Le cifre cumulative 1850–2024 riguardano: The cumulative figures for 1850–2024 concern fossil carbon only. Including historical land use the ranking changes significantly.
html.Tutti i valori sono arrotondati per la l: All values are rounded for readability. Before quoting one, check the exact figure at the primary source indicated above: the NOAA series and the Global Carbon Budget are revised with every edition.
html.Analisi divulgativa sul bilancio globale: A plain-language analysis of the global carbon budget. The data come from the Global Carbon Project, the NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory and Our World in Data. Budget: Global Carbon Budget 2025. Mauna Loa series: read from NOAA at every load, with the values saved on 12 September 2026 as a fallback.

html.La curva di Mauna Loa non misura quanto: The Mauna Loa curve does not measure what we emit. It measures what is left over after the oceans and vegetation have taken their share.

html.Concentrazione di CO2 negli ultimi 800 m: CO2 concentration over the last 800 thousand years measured in Antarctic ice cores: it swings between 170 and 300 parts per million following the ice ages, never going above 300. At the far right the curve rises vertically to today's 427 ppm.
html.Tre pannelli allineati sugli anni dal 20: Three panels aligned on the years from 2016 to 2026. Top: the monthly concentration at Mauna Loa rises from 402 to about 430 ppm with the seasonal swing clearly visible. Middle: the bars of annual growth, around 2 or 3 ppm a year, with 2016, 2023 and 2024 above 3 ppm and 2025 at 2.23; the decade average is 2.56. Bottom: the global temperature anomaly, from 1.17 degrees in 2016 to 1.42 in 2024 and 1.29 in 2025, with the peaks in the same years when CO2 grew most.
html.Anomalia della temperatura media globale: Global mean temperature anomaly from 1850 to 2025 relative to the 1850-1900 average: it fluctuates around zero until the 1970s, then rises to 1.42 degrees in 2024 and falls to 1.29 in 2025. The 1.5 degree threshold is marked by a dashed line just above.
html.Diagramma di flusso: 40,9 GtCO2 emesse o: Flow diagram: 40.9 GtCO2 emitted every year split into 11.8 absorbed by the ocean, 8.7 by vegetation and 20.4 that stay in the atmosphere.
html.Confronto fra la concentrazione osservat: Comparison between the observed concentration, which reaches 427 ppm in 2025, and the one there would have been without any absorption by oceans and vegetation, which would reach 574 ppm. The gap between the two curves grows over time.
html.Confronto fra il tasso di crescita della: Comparison between the CO2 growth rate at Mauna Loa and in the global mean from 2021 to 2025. In 2023 Mauna Loa reads 3.32 against 2.70 for the global mean; in 2024 the two swap over, 3.33 against 3.76; in 2025 both fall, 2.23 and 2.06.
html.Emissioni fossili mondiali dal 1990 al 2: World fossil emissions from 1990 to 2024: they rise from 22.7 to 38.6 billion tonnes. Marked are the signature of the protocol in 1997 at 24.4, entry into force in 2005 at 29.6 and the end of the first commitment period in 2012 at 35.0.

html.Due risposte controintuitive. Gli eserci: Two counter-intuitive answers. Armies in peacetime emit far more than the wars they fight. And inside a war the weapons weigh almost nothing: what counts is what they hit, and what then has to be rebuilt. Together they are worth about 5% of the world's greenhouse gases. These are the least solid estimates on this page, and they are floors, not measurements.
html.Quanto fa sul totale di un anno: How much it comes to in a year
html.<b>Cinque quadretti su cento.</b> Tanto: Five squares out of a hundred. That is the combined weight of the peacetime military apparatus, 4.8%, and the two wars for which a count exists, 0.2%, out of the 57.7 billion tonnes of greenhouse gases the world emitted in 2024. The first figure has a wide range, between 2.8 and 6.1%; the second is almost all Ukraine, and does not include the conflicts nobody has counted.
html.Durante la guerra le emissioni dichiarat: During the war the emissions declared by Syria fell, because oil production collapsed by more than a quarter. Meanwhile the damage was piling up elsewhere: putting the destroyed houses back up alone is worth about 22 MtCO₂, and it will arrive in the years of reconstruction. In official accounts a war can look like a climate policy, which is another reason why the share alongside is a floor.
html.Come sono fatte quelle due percentuali: How those two percentages are built
html.Il denominatore è il totale mondiale di: The denominator is the world total of all greenhouse gases in 2024, 57.7 GtCO₂e, from the UNEP emissions gap report. The 4.8% is the 2,750 MtCO₂e of the armies: the authors of the estimate write 5.5%, computed on an older and lower world total, and the substance does not change. The 0.2% is the sum of what is attributed to each year of war: 78 MtCO₂e for Ukraine, four years divided by four, and 27 for the conflict between Israel and Gaza. The two weeks in Iran are worth another 5 MtCO₂e, a thousandth of the world total, and cannot be annualised. Neither figure includes the emissions of the fighting itself, which the authors of the estimate on armies explicitly say they left out.
html.4 novembre 2025: totale mondiale di tutt: 4 November 2025: world total of all greenhouse gases in 2024, 57.7 GtCO₂e, +2.3% on the year before. It is the denominator of the percentages in the section on wars.
html.<b>La quota sul totale mondiale, che man: The share of the world total, which was missing. The section on wars gave absolute figures and comparisons, but did not answer the most direct question: how much do armies and wars weigh on one year of emissions. Now it does, with the denominator stated: 57.7 billion tonnes of greenhouse gases in 2024, from the UNEP report. Five squares out of a hundred, of which 4.8 the military apparatus and 0.2 the two wars for which a count exists.

html.<b>Nel 2024 erano attivi 61 conflitti ar: In 2024 there were 61 active armed conflicts, the highest number since the end of the Second World War. Two have a carbon count: Ukraine and Gaza. For Iran there is a preliminary estimate; for Syria, Lebanon, Yemen and Sudan, nothing. Armies for their part do not report: the first exemptions came with the Kyoto Protocol in 1997, since 2015 the Paris Agreement makes reporting voluntary, and the United States, China and Russia do not publish complete data. And even where a count exists, it counts greenhouse gases alone.
html.Anche i conti migliori misurano una cosa: Even the best accounts measure one thing only, greenhouse gases. Left out are the mines that make fields unfarmable, the heavy metals in the soil — lead, zinc, chromium, arsenic around Sumy —, the PFAS and asbestos lifted from the rubble, the dioxins of the fires, the crude that ended up in the Persian Gulf. That is not climate, it is a different damage, and none of the percentages on this page include it. Vegetation fires are left out too: in the sixteen countries with ongoing or recent conflicts, in 2020 alone, 1,456 MtCO₂e went into the air. Not all of it caused by war, but attributed to nobody.
html.Global Peace Index 2026: 61 conflitti ar: Global Peace Index 2026: 61 active armed conflicts in 2024, the highest number since the end of the Second World War.
html.<b>Controllo incrociato con un'inchiesta: Cross-checked against an investigation in Corriere della Sera. A reader pointed to Milena Gabanelli's Dataroom on the emissions of wars: every figure matches the ones on this page, because they come from the same studies. While we were at it, what was missing has been added: of the 61 conflicts active in 2024 only two have a carbon count, Lebanon joins the list of those that do not, and a note says that even the best accounts measure greenhouse gases alone, not the mines, the heavy metals or the oil at sea. One figure from the article was not taken up: the «59 wars, the highest number since 1945» are in fact 61 active conflicts, while 59 is the 2008 value of a different indicator.
html.Il denominatore è il totale mondiale di: The denominator is the world total of all greenhouse gases in 2024, 57.7 GtCO₂e, from the UNEP emissions gap report. The 4.8% is the 2,750 MtCO₂e of the armies: the authors of the estimate write 5.5%, computed on an older and lower world total, and the substance does not change. The 0.2% is the sum of what is attributed to each year of war: 78 MtCO₂e for Ukraine, four years divided by four, and 27 for the conflict between Israel and Gaza. The two weeks in Iran are worth another 5 MtCO₂e, a thousandth of the world total, and cannot be annualised.
html.Il 5,5% degli eserciti comprende le guer: Does the armies' 5.5% include the wars? No
html.È la domanda che quel numero si tira die: It is the question that number drags behind it, and the answer changes what the sum means. The 4.8% is the apparatus that stands there anyway: fuel for vehicles, ships and aircraft, the bases, and above all the industry that builds and supplies them. Of that total only a fifth, 1% of world emissions, is fuel burned by the armed forces; the rest is the supply chain. The authors of the estimate write that it is conservative precisely because it leaves out the emissions of the fighting: what happens when the shooting starts is not in there.
html.Lo 0,2% delle guerre conta invece propri: The wars' 0.2% counts exactly that: fuel spent in battle, munitions, destroyed equipment to replace, burned buildings, reconstruction. The two figures measure different things, which is why they can be added without counting anything twice. A grey zone does exist — an army at war burns more than an army in barracks, and that extra could show up on both sides — but it is small next to the range of the first figure, which runs from 2.8 to 6.1%.
html.<b>Corretta una frase falsa sulle guerre: A false sentence about the wars corrected. It said that «neither of the two figures includes the fighting itself»: true for the armies' 4.8%, not for the wars' 0.2%, which counts the fighting very much indeed. In its place there is now the answer to the question that number drags behind it: the armies' 5.5% does not include the wars, it is the apparatus that stands there anyway, and of that total only a fifth is fuel burned by the armed forces, the rest is the industry that supplies them. That is why the two figures can be added without counting anything twice.
html.Delle 40,9 GtCO2 emesse ogni anno l'ocea: Of the 40.9 GtCO2 emitted each year the ocean absorbs 11.8, vegetation 8.7, and 20.4 stay in the air.
html.La curva di Mauna Loa non misura quanto: The Mauna Loa curve does not measure what we emit. It measures what is left over.
